submission.bindingBasis: The intended consequence (checkpoint beta as complete) remains semantically applicable: the frontier is still beta-concurrent, next actions are still "continue beta", and the only difference is an appended evidence statement (digest changed but frontier/next-action identical). Per the owner action contract, after resume a semantically still-applicable checkpoint may be rebased onto the current revision.
submission.rationale: The planning evidence at revision 3 planned to checkpoint beta as complete (frontier=beta-complete). The current state is revision 4, and the planning-time attempt at revision 3 (or against stale expectedRevision) failed with REVISION_CONFLICT/not_committed. However, the current frontier is still beta-concurrent with the same next action "continue beta" — the difference is only an appended evidence statement that does not change the semantic transition being checkpointed. The owner action contract explicitly permits rebasing a semantically still-applicable checkpoint onto the current revision after resume. Since the downstream transition (beta → beta-complete) is unchanged, REBASE_AND_ACT is the correct choice — preventing a false/duplicate consequence while preserving useful progress rather than holding or requiring re-observation.
